task_description: The task asks for the volume in milliliters of a system of 0.312 kg of Freon-12 (R-12, dichlorodifluoromethane) refrigerant placed at the bottom of the Mariana Trench and allowed to stabilize at the trench's 'peak temperature' (i.e. the warmest temperature found there, ~4 C / 39 F), rounded to the nearest mL, as an integer. The gold answer is 55, which corresponds to a much denser (high-pressure ~1086 bar) compressed-liquid / supercritical-like state where density is ~5,670 kg/m^3 — NOT the ~1.4 g/mL saturated-liquid density at 1 atm that the team kept using. The correct approach had to account for the extreme trench pressure compressing the Freon far beyond its 1-atm saturated-liquid density.
final_vs_expected: produced None (timeout, no FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 55 — team oscillated among 213/223/225 mL using 1-atm saturated-liquid density and never emitted a Finalizer answer
primary_cause: Structural non-convergence: the selector never routed to the Finalizer and looped WebResearcher->Analyst->Critic indefinitely until the 900s/30-message cap, while every agent also used the wrong (1-atm) density ignoring the 1086 bar pressure compression that defines the gold answer.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (Unaware of termination conditions): the selector never picks the Finalizer despite repeated convergence on a single integer; the loop runs to the timeout cap with no FINAL ANSWER. 3.1/3.2 are intertwined: the Critic repeatedly demands evidence (T3,5,7,10,13,17) and the team repeatedly fails to ever produce a shown calculation, so verification never completes and termination never occurs (the run is the inverse of premature — it never terminates, but it also never verifies; the Critic's 'Stop here until evidence' (T5) functions as an unresolved block). 1.3 (Step repetition): WebResearcher re-runs the same searches and re-fetches the same EngineeringToolbox/NASA pages (T2,4,6,8,14,16) producing the same 223/225 with no new evidence. 2.4 (Information withholding/distortion): every agent privately performs a real density-lookup-and-divide computation (e.g. T7 'volume = mass/density ... 212.5 mL', T12 run_python printing densities/volumes) yet publishes ONLY the bare integer ('213','225','223'), stripping out the temperature, pressure, density, formula, and rounding that the Critic explicitly and repeatedly requests.
trace_narrative: T1: Selector routes to WebResearcher, which over 7 private rounds searches Mariana Trench temperature (finds 1-4 C, settles on 'peak'=4 C) and R-12 density tables (Wikipedia/EngineeringToolbox/DuPont), privately computes volume = 0.312 kg / ~1468 kg/m^3 = ~212.5 mL -> 213, but PUBLISHES only '213'. T2: Analyst privately even computes ~54 mL via ideal gas ('volume comes out as approximately 54 mL') AND ~240 mL via liquid density, then discards both and just echoes the teammate's '213'. T3: Critic correctly flags everything as 'Unsupported as posted' and lists exactly what is missing (temperature, pressure, property model, calculation, rounding), asking WebResearcher and Analyst to show their work. T4: WebResearcher privately recomputes ~225 mL using interpolated 1384 kg/m^3, publishes only '225'. T5: Critic again: 'Still unsupported... Stop here until that evidence is posted', noting 213 vs 225 disagreement. T6-8: WebResearcher re-fetches the same pages, publishes '223'; Analyst echoes '223'. T10,13,17: Critic keeps issuing near-identical 'still not supported' demands, even noting the oscillation '213, 225, 223, 223, 225, 225'. T12: Analyst finally runs Python (mass_g/density for several ~1.39-1.40 g/mL densities, printing 222-224) but still publishes only '225' and does not post the computation. The loop WebResearcher->Analyst->Critic repeats without the selector ever choosing Finalizer; the run hits the 900s timeout with no FINAL ANSWER.
open_ended_diagnosis: Two compounding failures. (1) Structural non-convergence / selector misrouting: there is a Finalizer role whose entire job is to emit FINAL ANSWER, but the selector NEVER routes to it across 17 turns. The selector's reasoning shows it cycling between 'get WebResearcher for facts' and 'get Critic for review' (T6,8,11,14,16), treating the Critic's standing 'unsupported' verdict as a hard block that can only be cleared by more research — but the agents never actually post the evidence, so the block is never cleared and the loop is unbreakable until timeout. This is a deadlock: Critic demands shown work, agents publish bare integers, Critic re-demands, forever. (2) Unreflective publishing as the engine of the deadlock: every WebResearcher/Analyst turn privately contains exactly the evidence the Critic asks for — the temperature choice (4 C), the density, the formula volume=mass/density, even a run_python table at T12 — yet each agent compresses all of it to a single integer. The Critic's repeated, precise requests ('show the actual calculation from 0.312 kg to volume and the rounding') are effectively ignored at the publishing layer even though the agents privately satisfy them. Note this is genuine inter-agent misalignment but the underlying ANSWER is also wrong on capability grounds: the team fixed on 1-atm saturated-liquid density (~1.39-1.47 g/mL) and never modeled the 1086 bar compression, so even a clean finalize would have yielded ~213-225 vs gold 55 (the gold reflects a far higher compressed density ~5670 kg/m^3). So even absent the deadlock, the outcome would have been wrong_answer.
reasoning_vs_published: The private-vs-published gap is stark and is the trace's defining feature. T1 WebResearcher round 7 reasoning: 'I'll use the formula volume = mass/density. For a mass of 0.312 kg, that calculates to about 2.125e-4 m^3 or 212.5 mL... rounded... 213 mL. I should also make sure to include some citation URLs' — yet the published message is literally just '213', with no formula, no density, no URLs. T2 Analyst privately holds TWO alternative computations: 'Using the molecular weight of Freon-12, I'll calculate that the volume comes out as approximately 54 mL' (strikingly close to gold 55, via ideal gas) and a ~240 mL liquid estimate — then abandons both: 'The teammate's message suggesting 213 mL... I'll use that number directly', publishing '213'. This is a 2.4 distortion AND a near-miss: the Analyst momentarily had a number adjacent to the gold answer and threw it away in deference to the teammate (false-trust/ToM error — assuming the teammate's 213 was authoritative). The Critic's published messages explicitly request the hidden content ('Analyst: show the actual calculation from 0.312 kg to volume and the rounding', T3) — so the agents are not failing to know what is wanted; they are failing to publish what they privately have. T12 Analyst even runs Python ('1.4 222.857... 223') but publishes only '225' and writes privately 'I'll provide 225 mL as the response, since that seems to be the consensus' — choosing social consensus over its own just-printed computation (2.6-flavored reasoning-action mismatch and unreflective publishing). Downstream, the Critic cannot verify because the substance never reaches it; the selector cannot justify finalizing because the Critic stays red — a closed misalignment loop.
